q: 1. Addition of pozzolana to ordinary Portland cement causes
explain: Pozzolana addition actually decreases heat of hydration, may slightly improve workability, and doesn't directly increase early strength, so none of the given effects apply — the correct textbook effect (reduced heat of hydration) is not listed, hence 'none of these'.

q: 2. Setting time of cement increases by adding
explain: Gypsum is added during cement manufacture specifically to retard (delay/increase) the setting time by controlling the reaction of tricalcium aluminate with water.

q: 3. Setting time of cement decreases by adding
explain: Calcium chloride is a well-known accelerating admixture that speeds up hydration, thereby decreasing (shortening) the setting time of cement.

q: 4. The cement concrete, from which entrained air and excess water are removed after placing it in position, is called
explain: In vacuum concrete, a vacuum process is applied after placing to remove excess water and entrapped air, increasing density and early strength.

q: 5. A suitable admixture added at the time of preparing the concrete mix, makes the concrete
explain: Different admixtures are available to impart different properties, so depending on the admixture chosen, concrete can be made water-proof, acid-proof, or of higher strength.

q: 6. Addition of sugar in concrete results in
options: increase in setting time by about 1 hr
increase in setting time by about 4 hr
decrease in setting time by about 1 hr
decrease in setting time by about 4 hr
explain: Sugar acts as a retarder in concrete; it delays the setting time significantly, by about 4 hours, when added in small quantities.

q: 7. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: calcium chloride acts as a retarder
gypsum (calcium sulphate) acts as an accelerator
gypsum (calcium sulphate) acts as a retarder
calcium chloride acts as an accelerator
explain: Gypsum retards the setting time of cement by controlling C3A hydration, while calcium chloride acts as an accelerator, speeding up the setting; hence both (c) and (d) are correct.

q: 8. The strength of concrete using air entraining cement gets reduced by
explain: Entrained air, while improving workability and frost resistance, reduces the compressive strength of concrete typically by about 10-15%.

q: 9. Reduction in the quantity of mixing water which is possibly by the use of plasticizers and admixtures varies from
explain: Ordinary plasticizing admixtures typically allow a water reduction of about 5% to 15% while maintaining the same workability.

q: 10. Most commonly used material for accelerating hardening of the concrete is
explain: Calcium chloride is the most widely used chemical accelerator, added to speed up the setting and early strength development of concrete.

q: 11. The entrained air in concrete
explain: Per the answer key, entrained air is stated to decrease resistance to weathering here — note this differs from typical air-entrainment theory (which normally improves frost/weathering resistance), but the correct option as marked in the source is (c).

q: 12. Admixtures which causes early setting and hardening of concrete are called
explain: Accelerating admixtures are specifically added to speed up the setting and early hardening/strength-gain of concrete.

q: 13. The most commonly used admixture which prolongs the setting and hardening time is
explain: Note: calcium chloride is generally an accelerator; however, per the book's listed answer for this question, it is identified as the admixture that prolongs setting/hardening time.

q: 14. The entrained air in concrete
explain: Entrained air bubbles act like tiny ball bearings within the mix, improving the flow and workability of fresh concrete.

q: 15. While designing an air entrained concrete
options: an allowance for the entrained air is made
strength of the concretes, is reduced
explain: In air-entrained concrete mix design, a specific allowance/adjustment is made in the mix proportions to account for the volume of entrained air voids introduced into the mix.

q: 16. The IS recommend the use of calcium chloride as accelerating admixture in
explain: Calcium chloride, being corrosive to embedded steel, is recommended by IS only for plain (unreinforced) concrete and reinforced concrete under controlled conditions — not for prestressed concrete, where corrosion risk to tendons is critical.

q: 17. Air entrainment in concrete increases:
explain: Entrained air bubbles improve the flow characteristics of fresh concrete, thereby increasing its workability, though it typically reduces strength and unit weight.

q: 18. A suitable admixture added at the time of preparing for concrete mix makes the concrete:
explain: Depending on the specific admixture used, concrete properties can be tailored to be water-proof, acid-proof, or of higher strength, so all these outcomes are achievable.

q: 19. Addition of air entraining agents to concrete increases all of the following EXCEPT
explain: Air-entraining agents improve workability and resistance to weathering effects during curing, and reduce bleeding rather than increasing it, making bleeding the exception.

q: 20. A suitable admixture added at the time of preparing the concrete mix, makes the concrete .........
explain: Depending on the type used, admixtures can impart waterproofing, acid resistance, or increased strength to concrete — so all of these are possible outcomes.

q: 21. Pozzolanic properties exist in
explain: All these materials - shales, fly ash, pumicite, and diatomaceous clay - are known to possess pozzolanic properties, meaning they can react with calcium hydroxide to form cementitious compounds.

q: 22. Common sugar can be suitably used
options: to delay the setting time of concrete
to accelerate the setting time of concrete
to increase the strength of concrete
explain: Sugar, in small controlled doses, acts as a retarder that delays the setting time of concrete by interfering with the hydration process.

q: 23. Air entraining in the concrete increases
explain: Entrained air bubbles act as tiny ball bearings within the mix, improving the flow and workability of fresh concrete.

q: 24. Gypsum is used as admixture in concrete to increase the property of concrete
explain: Gypsum is interground with clinker/added to cement primarily to retard/regulate the initial setting time, acting as a retarder.

q: 25. Calcium chloride is used as admixture in concrete to increase the property of concrete
explain: Calcium chloride is a well-known chemical accelerator that speeds up the hydration process and early strength gain of concrete.

q: 26. Calcium chloride as an accelerating admixture is not recommended for use with
explain: With high alumina cement, calcium chloride can cause flash setting and a serious loss of ultimate strength, so its use is specifically avoided in that case.

q: 27. To improve the certain properties of concrete, admixture is used at the time of
explain: Admixtures are dosed into the mix during the mixing stage so that they are uniformly dispersed and can act effectively throughout the concrete.

q: 28. An admixture
options: is a basic ingredient of concrete
offers improvement not economically attained by adjusting mix proportions
is a substitute for good concreting practice
is beneficial to the properties of concrete when used in large quantities
explain: An admixture is defined as a material used to achieve special properties (workability, setting time, etc.) that could not be economically obtained just by varying the basic mix proportions.

q: 29. An admixture could be used to
explain: Different classes of admixtures can accelerate setting, enhance strength, or improve workability, so admixtures collectively serve all these purposes.

q: 30. An accelerator shortens all of the following except
explain: An accelerator speeds up setting, curing duration, and permits earlier formwork removal, but it does not 'shorten' strength — strength is a magnitude, not a time-based quantity, so it is the exception.

q: 31. Addition of retarder to concrete decreases all of the following except
explain: A retarder slows the rate of hydration and rate of strength development, but it does not necessarily decrease workability (in fact it can be prolonged) or ultimate compressive strength, making this option the exception.

q: 32. The entrained air in the concrete
explain: Entrained air bubbles act like small ball bearings, improving the flow of fresh concrete and thereby increasing its workability.

q: 33. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
explain: Since different types of admixtures individually achieve acceleration of hydration, waterproofing, acid resistance and strength gain, none of the listed statements is incorrect on its own.

q: 34. The presence of calcium chloride in water
options: causes little effect on quality of concrete
explain: Calcium chloride, when present in mixing water, acts as an accelerator that speeds up both the setting and the hardening of cement, so both a and b occur.
